title: P.N.03
subtitle: A mercenary moves to a different rhythm
summary: P.N.03 is Capcom's third-person action game, first released for GameCube in Japan on 27 March 2003.
body: P.N.03 is Capcom's third-person action game, first released for GameCube in Japan on 27 March 2003. Directed by Shinji Mikami, it follows mercenary Vanessa Z. Schneider through a colony where defensive robots have turned hostile. Vanessa's Aegis suit fires energy from her hands and supports elaborate evasive movement. The game builds its identity around the pauses between attacks: standing still to shoot makes recognising an enemy's next action essential before deciding when to move or return fire.

Robots follow attack patterns signalled by movement and sound. Rolls, spins and cover let Vanessa avoid their fire, but moving and shooting are separate actions. The player must create a safe opening rather than continuously attack while running around the room. Energy Drives provide powerful attacks and temporary protection at the cost of stored energy. Destroying enemies in quick succession also starts a scoring chain, encouraging the player to learn an efficient route through a group without taking unnecessary damage.

Points earned in missions buy new suits, upgrades and Energy Drives. Trial missions offer more opportunities to practise and gather resources between the main stages. Each room becomes a small arrangement of threats to read, and another attempt can turn a hesitant advance into a more fluent sequence of dodges and attacks. Shusaku Uchiyama and Makoto Tomozawa's electronic score accompanies Vanessa's rhythmic animation. That combination gives the game a particular physical character, even when its environments and enemies repeat familiar structures.
story_headings: A mercenary moves to a different rhythm
Watch the machine before answering its attack
Repeat the room with a better plan
